_comment: Data/Content/week-<n>/day-<n>.json - ONE day of the course, imported from four .ipynb notebooks by scripts/import-notebooks.ts. GENERATED: never hand-edit; the notebooks in the training repo are the master. A day has UP TO 4 parts. A missing _1 becomes a generated placeholder so the TypeScript tab stays present (Week 1 days 1-4). A missing _3 is simply absent - Week 1 Day 1 is theory plus practice and has no second concept notebook. Nothing downstream may assume four parts.

title._comment: Day title, taken from the _2 notebook's H1 with the 'Week N, Day N.2 - ' prefix stripped.
title.value: From recorder to real code: actions on a form

locked._comment: true for weeks not yet authored (3-8 in the first release). A locked day imports fully but the UI shows it greyed and refuses to open it.

parts._comment: 1 to 4, in order. part 1 = TypeScript prerequisites, 2 and 3 = Playwright concepts, 4 = practice. Week 1 Day 1 has only parts 2 and 4.

kind._comment: prerequisite = the _1 TypeScript check-in. concept = _2 and _3. practice = _4. generated-prerequisite = emitted by the importer where no _1 notebook exists.

tab_label._comment: Short label for the tab bar. Derived from the title, not a bare 'Part 2'.

source_notebook._comment: Path relative to the training repo root. null for a generated part.

has_runnable_code._comment: false when the notebook carries no example cells (e.g. Week 1 Day 1.2, a pure-theory day). Drives the editor's empty state.

blocks._comment: Ordered content blocks, in DOCUMENT ORDER. Markdown blocks render as prose; example blocks get a 'Load into editor' button; your-turn blocks render as a 'Try it' callout; a problem-ref block marks where a practice problem sits, its text being the problem number. Rendering all prose before all problems put the closing note above Problem 1. The last three types are never parsed from a notebook - they are merged in from an authored lesson overlay (see lesson_overlay_format.json) and give every lesson the same shape: at-a-glance opens it, checkpoint and recap close it.

text._comment: Markdown source for a markdown block; TypeScript source for example and your-turn blocks; the problem number as a string for problem-ref; markdown for at-a-glance and recap; the question itself for a checkpoint.

starter._comment: your-turn ONLY: the preceding example's setup (harness launch through its first page.goto), so 'Try it' opens the editor on working navigation rather than a bare comment. null for every other block type, and for a your-turn whose example never opened a page.

variation._comment: your-turn ONLY: an authored same-concept, different-scenario prompt (Data/Content/variations/w<week>d<day>.json, keyed 'p<part>_yt<n>'), replacing the generic 'retype from memory' text once written. null = not yet authored, and the generic prompt renders instead - the reveal-solution pattern, not a broken callout.

prompt.value: Do the same thing, but sign in as Katy instead of Leela.

checkpoint._comment: checkpoint ONLY: the options, the answer and why. Merged in from Data/Content/lessons/w<week>d<day>.json. Formative and never scored - nothing is written to progress, so a wrong answer costs only the reading. null for every other block type.

options._comment: 2-5 answers. Every one has to be defensible from the lesson's own text.

explanation._comment: Shown after answering, right or wrong - the reason, not just the verdict.

problems._comment: Present ONLY on a practice part. Weeks 1-4 and 8 give 3 labelled problems; weeks 5-7 give 7-8 numbered exercises with no difficulty label, so `difficulty` is nullable and the count is NOT fixed at 3. `solution` is authored by hand - the source notebooks carry empty stubs - and is null until a week has been authored.

number._comment: 1-based within the part. Runs to 8 in weeks 5-7.

difficulty._comment: null where the source numbers its exercises without labelling them (weeks 5-7). 'Reflection, no code' is normalised to 'Reflection'.

statement._comment: Markdown: what to build, where, and how you will know it worked.

stub._comment: The starter cell, e.g. '// Problem 1 - your code here.'. For a non-Reflection problem, prefixed at import time with the day's own setup boilerplate (the last example's launch + goto, from parts 2-3) so the editor is never a blank comment - see extractBoilerplate() in scripts/notebook-parse.ts.

solution._comment: Authored model answer in MARKDOWN, revealed on a deliberate click. Markdown rather than bare code because many problems are reflection, research or terminal work, where the worked answer is prose; code answers carry their own fence. null = not yet authored, and the reveal button is absent rather than broken.
